question.text: The normal to the curve $y=x^{2}-x+1$, drawn at the points with the abscissa $x_{1}=0, x_{2}=-1$ and $x_{3}=5 / 2$

solution.text:
Given equation of curve.
$$
\begin{aligned}
y &=x^{2}-x+1 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x-1
\end{aligned}
$$
Slope of normal $=\frac{1}{1-2 x}$
Now, at $x_{1}=0, y_{1}=1$
$\therefore$ Slope of normal at $(0,1)=1$
$\therefore$ Equation of normal, $y-1=1(x-0)$ $\Rightarrow \quad x-y+1=0$
At $x_{2}=-1, y_{2}=3$
Slope of normal at $(-1,3)=\frac{1}{3}$ Equation of normal, $y-3=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)$
$\Rightarrow \quad 3 y-9=x+1$
$x-3 y+10=0$
At $x_{3}=\frac{5}{2}, y_{3}=\frac{19}{4}$
Slope of normal at $\left(\frac{2}{5}, \frac{19}{4}\right)=-\frac{1}{4}$
Equation of normal, $y-\frac{19}{4}=-\frac{1}{4}\left(x-\frac{5}{2}\right)$
$\begin{array}{lr}\Rightarrow & x+4 y=\frac{43}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x+8 y=43\end{array}$
Here, intersecting point of Eqs.(i) and (ii) is 
(ii) is $\left(\frac{7}{2}, \frac{9}{2}\right)$ and normal (iii) passes through it. Hence, normals are concurrent.
